title: Moon base: the 354-hour night
note: Every sentence comes from the goal's facts in the app (bottlenecks b3.1 and b3.3, the pending promise 'NASA astronauts would visit the Moon's south pole by 2030'). Qualifiers are kept: about, mostly, in some seasons, has said, yet.

shots.job: This shot shows a lit habitat through 38 hours of a real dark spell, so the viewer understands how long a night is for anything that must stay on.
This shot shows a person outside the lit habitat in the dark, so the viewer understands what cannot be switched off.
This shot shows one real month of sunlight sweeping the south pole's ridges, so the viewer understands why the pole is where a base could find power.

This shot shows the same dark spell from closer, 30 hours passing with only the windows lit, so the viewer understands that even this ridge goes dark for days and nothing with a crew has been through it.
This shot shows a person on the same ridge in the low Sun of the sunny season, so the viewer understands what has been promised for 2030.

lines.say: A night on the Moon lasts about three hundred and fifty-four hours.

lines.say: Small landers have survived it by mostly shutting down.
Some ridges at the south pole get sunlight most of the time.

lines.say: Even the best go dark for days in some seasons.
